clauses.reason: The sole clause commands that "Executive Order No. 12217 is revoked." A revocation takes its whole effect when the order is issued, so the clause was performed and spent on issue, on the signing date August 11, 1983 (the order states no later effective date; the Federal Register printed it on August 15, 1983). The revoked order's absence thereafter is an accrued effect, not a continuing command of EO 12437. No earlier ending is possible and no later amendment, supersession or revocation of EO 12437 is held.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12437 of August 11, 1983 (Fuel Use Prohibitions, 48 FR 36801) is a single paragraph whose only command is that "Executive Order No. 12217 is revoked." It creates no continuing duty, office, standard or deadline. A command that revokes another order is carried out when the order issues, so the order's own operative force was spent on issue (signing date August 11, 1983; filed for publication 8-12-83, printed August 15, 1983). Status recommended: no. The only clause is therefore terminated on 1983-08-11 by performance of its own terms. The consequence that survives, EO 12217 remaining revoked, is an accrued effect of the revocation and is not a continuing command of EO 12437. The Federal Register disposition note held for this order records that it revokes EO 12217 of June 18, 1980, and the held U.S. Code text at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t42-s8373.txt recites that EO 12217 was revoked by this order; both recite the revocation and neither amends or ends EO 12437. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog found no later instrument that amends, supersedes or revokes EO 12437, and a search of the held texts for its number found no citation in any other held text. No later event is claimed.

savings.reason: The only legal consequence that survives is that Executive Order No. 12217 stands revoked. That is an accrued effect of the revocation carried out on issue; nothing in the order's text reserves, saves or continues any right, duty or program of EO 12437 itself, and the order contains no savings clause.
